steps.title: Read a ticket as a story
steps.text: This ticket asks for a page that tells a ticket the way this one does: a picture to start, a short section for each thing it must do, drawn first, then the code it builds on. It takes a few minutes to scroll.

steps.title: Today, a ticket is one long document
steps.text: You review it in a document that holds everything at once. The code it will change is only a link in its notes, so you have to picture it.

steps.title: This ticket asks for a story instead
steps.text: A picture, then a section for each part of the ticket, and a panel that shows what the step you are reading is about.

steps.title: Five things it must do
steps.text: Each has a section below: what the ticket says, a drawing, the code it builds on as it stands today, and how the run will show it. Nine decisions follow.

find: A ticket can be published as a story page
steps.title: A section for each criterion
steps.text: The page itself: a ticket, told before it is built, with one section for each thing it must do.

steps.title: How a story is laid out
steps.text: A picture and a welcome, one section per criterion in the ticket's order, the decisions, then the code it cites.

steps.title: Inside a section
steps.text: What the ticket says, a drawing of how it works, the code it builds on with its lines lit, then the check the run must pass.

steps.title: How a page gets made
steps.text: The booking clerk makes a story for every ticket it prepares, once the follow-up lands, and any session makes one when you ask. The story and its drawings are written, Codex draws the picture, and the builder checks them against the code and the ticket and writes one page, linked beside the draft.

steps.title: Where the instructions go
steps.text: The review-pages skill holds two pages today, a review page and a code viewer, then its rules. A section on story pages joins them.

steps.title: The rule that points sessions there
steps.text: This rule sends a session to the review-pages skill to show a change or a ticket's code. It will name the story page for a ticket's story.

find: C1 Build a story for this ticket
steps.title: How the run must show it
steps.text: The run builds a story for this ticket and one for #271 at its own base, and checks each opens with its picture, then has one section per criterion, in order.

find: The story opens with a picture
D7 (proposed) Codex draws the picture
steps.title: A picture to start
steps.text: The story opens on a picture of what the ticket asks for, in the poster's style. Decision 7 says who draws it.

steps.title: How the picture is made
steps.text: The session describes the scene, and Codex draws it with the postmaster poster as its style. The session looks at it, lettering included, before it goes on the page, and asks again if a word comes out wrong.

find: C2 A story whose opening names a picture
steps.title: How the run must show it
steps.text: A stand-in picture tool proves the page takes what it returns. One real Codex call, made by hand, shows the style and the lettering.

find: The panel beside the story always shows
steps.title: The panel follows the outlined step
steps.text: Whichever step is outlined, the panel beside it shows what that step tells.

steps.title: The reading line
steps.text: On a phone the panel holds the top half and the steps scroll beneath it. The step crossing the reading line is outlined, and the panel shows its scene.

find: C3 The function that picks
steps.title: How the run must show it
steps.text: Choosing the step is a plain function, tested for a step on the line, between two steps, above the first and below the last, at phone and iPad sizes.

find: Each section draws what it describes
D8 (given by the user) Each part is drawn
steps.title: Drawn before code
steps.text: Each section draws what it describes before it shows any code. Decision 8, yours, is the reason.

steps.title: The order the builder keeps
steps.text: A section whose first code step comes before any drawing is refused, so a story cannot skip the pictures.

find: C4 The story for this ticket
steps.title: How the run must show it
steps.text: The story for this ticket passes. The same story with the first drawing of criterion 1 removed is refused, and the refusal names that section.

find: The code the ticket cites is shown
D9 (proposed) The story shows the code
steps.title: The code it cites, shown
steps.text: Every line the ticket's notes point to is shown as it stands today, on a step or in the list at the end.

steps.title: Every cited line goes somewhere
steps.text: This ticket cites 19 lines, and this page shows all of them on its steps. It also links one whole file, which the list at the end names.

steps.title: Cleaned before it is shown
steps.text: Before any code is shown, the builder removes email addresses with this function from the review page's builder. The one above it names each file's language for highlighting.

find: C5 The coverage test reads the links
steps.title: How the run must show it
steps.text: A test reads the ticket's links and the page's rows: no cited line may be on neither. Removing a code step moves its lines into the list.

find: D1 (given by the user) Once this lands
steps.title: Decision 1, yours: the clerk will make them
steps.text: With this ticket, a session makes a story when you ask. A follow-up then has the booking clerk make one for every ticket it prepares.

steps.title: Now, and after the follow-up
steps.text: The clerk's story will sit beside the draft's document, where you still comment and edit, and a setting can turn it off.

find: D2 (proposed) The page is for reading
steps.title: Decision 2: for reading
steps.text: No comments and no verdict on the page; you answer in the chat and edit the ticket in its document, as now.

find: D3 (given by the user) The page looks and scrolls
steps.title: Decision 3, yours: as the trials
steps.text: The look and scroll you chose, with drawings that change as the steps go.

find: D4 (given by the user) The start is simple
steps.title: Decision 4, yours: an inviting start
steps.text: A picture and a plain welcome first, and the ticket's text after.

find: D5 (proposed) The ticket's words appear
steps.title: Decision 5: a step at a time
steps.text: Only the words a step is about, set large, and the whole ticket near the end, as this page does.

find: D6 (proposed) Markdown files among
steps.title: Decision 6: Markdown as text
steps.text: Instructions and runbooks show as formatted text, as the skill and the rule did above. Code stays code.

find: D7 (proposed) Codex draws the picture
steps.title: Decision 7: Codex draws the picture
steps.text: On your ChatGPT plan, with nothing to paste. Each picture counts against the Codex limit your Codex lanes use.

find: The story page is a page the review-pages skill publishes
It starts from the trials' files
steps.title: What binds the run
steps.text: Claude Code only, a phone and an iPad in light and dark, nothing private, and no fixture run. It waits for #321 to put the trials' files in the repository.

steps.title: Everything you sign
steps.text: Here is the whole part you sign, in one place, now that you have seen each piece.

steps.title: The code it cites
steps.text: The ticket's notes cite {changed} lines of today's code, and {shown} of them are on the steps above. It also links one whole file, named in the panel.
